snippet.title: The Untold Story Of The Bellaire House - Ohio
snippet.description:

Like a mouse falling into a pit of snakes an unsuspecting family disturbed a slumbering force and became enshrouded in a fog of darkness. From paranormal activity, demonic manifestations and dark seances. There is a lot to this Ohio story. This is untold story of the Bellaire House and the terrifying malevolent entities that dwell within it's walls.

snippet.title: Inside Bellaire, Ohio | How Did It Get Like This?
snippet.description: Inside Bellaire, Ohio...how did it get to this point?  Once a thriving area with glass manufacturing, steel, coal mining, railroads, now a shadow of what it was used to be.  After the industrial decline this area has lost a significant part of its population, and has continued to suffer as no recovery is really in sight.  Very interesting place though, with lots of rich history inside.  The movie "The Silence of the Lambs" filmed a memorable scene on the old Bellaire Bridge.  I also check out the Great Stone Viaduct, and even see the haunted Bellaire House along the way...So many cool things so let's get to it!

snippet.title: Notorious 'Devil in Bellaire' seeks parole after 30 years for horrific double murder
snippet.description:
It was a story that sent chills down the spine of the Ohio Valley.

After 30 years in prison, Nathan Brooks, who murdered his parents as a teenager, will be up for parole next month.

Many remember Brooks as the “Devil in Bellaire" and the "Dark Prince of Belmont County."

Brooks was 17 when he brutally stabbed his mother and shot his father in their home in September 1995. He later decapitated his father with a hacksaw and placed his head in a punch bowl as part of a satanic ritual.

"It was a big story back then, still is. You know, you don't forget it," said Belmont County Sheriff James Zusack, who had just joined the office four years prior to the murders.

Wherever Brooks went, Zusack went.

"Any type of doctor's visit, psychology visit, court. I always rode in the back of a cop car with him without a weapon," he said.

Zusack recalls gothic people from Columbus visiting brooks in the Belmont County Jail.

"He was the type of person that looked normal,” Zusack said. “He acted normal, looked normal, but there was just something. You could tell he worshipped Satan."

snippet.title: We Found the Runaway Train Filming Location! | Bellaire Viaduct
snippet.description:
Here’s the corrected description with the movie title fixed to **Unstoppable**:

In this episode of **Miles and Memories**, we head to **Bellaire, Ohio** to explore the historic **Bellaire Viaduct**, a location connected to the filming of **Unstoppable**, starring **Denzel Washington** and **Chris Pine**.

We walk around the viaduct, take in this impressive structure up close, and share the history and significance of this well-known local landmark. If you enjoy movie filming locations, railroad history, and discovering unique places across small-town America, this is a stop you won’t want to miss.

There’s something exciting about visiting a real place tied to a major Hollywood film, especially one as memorable as **Unstoppable**.

Come along as we explore the **Bellaire Viaduct** and uncover another fascinating piece of Ohio Valley history.

snippet.title: Driving around Bellaire, Ohio
snippet.description:
Bellaire is a village in Belmont County, Ohio, United States. It is part of the Wheeling, West Virginia Metropolitan Statistical Area, and Wheeling is across the Ohio to the east. The population was 4,278 at the 2010 census, having had its peak in 1920. The city is located along the Ohio River.

The Bellaire toll bridge (now abandoned and closed) was filmed in the 1991 motion picture The Silence of the Lambs. The curved railroad viaduct and bridge over the Ohio, the B & O Railroad Viaduct, were featured in the 2010 film Unstoppable and is a registered historic structure. A logo featuring the historic stone bridge is featured on official village paperwork as well as on police uniforms, and was designed by former resident Michael A. Massa, creator of the Belmont county seal, under the Administration of former City Mayor Fitch.
